subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does the gateway security owner agree that predictable event sequence numbers do not cross an authentication or authorization boundary, allowing this issue to close unless a concrete exploit proof is supplied?
rationale: The source contract contradicts the proposed attack mechanism, but the protected security label requires explicit human ownership of the final security-boundary disposition.

options.title: Confirm and close
options.body: Confirm that event sequence numbers are ordering-only metadata and close unless a current-main cross-boundary proof is provided.

options.title: Request exploit proof
options.body: Keep the issue open briefly and require a reproducible unauthenticated, cross-device, or cross-connection injection transcript before considering code changes.

options.title: Commission protocol audit
options.body: Perform a broader authenticated WebSocket integrity review if maintainers suspect a different message-forgery boundary not described by this report.

recommendation.title: Confirm and close
recommendation.body: Confirm that event sequence numbers are ordering-only metadata and close unless a current-main cross-boundary proof is provided.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail spans the gateway-client extraction, protocol lifecycle, and adjacent gateway security behavior.
